newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Two French aid workers freed in Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Two French aid workers freed in Afghanistan.

text.p: Two French aid workers held by the purist Islamic Taleban were found guilty and released on Wednesday after a trial in the Afghan capital Kabul, eyewitnesses said.

The two men, Frederic Michel and Daniel Llorente, who work for the Paris-based charity Action Contre la Faim (ACF - Action Against Hunger), were sentenced by a three-man tribunal to one month in prison and ordered to leave the country.

"Frederic Robert Michel and Jose Daniel Llorente, by the decision of the court, will serve one month of imprisonment from the date of their detention, and also be given an order to leave the country," said Judge Maulawi Gul Mohammed at the end of the three-hour hearing.

An official in the Foreign Ministry said that since the two men had already been held for almost a month they would be released immediately and allowed to leave Kabul with a delegation from the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC), which had interceded on their behalf.
Five Afghan staff who were arrested in connection with the same incident received sentences of one and a half months imprisonment with between nine and 29 lashes.
The seven were arrested in connection with a farewell party given by the charity's female workers for their local women staffers on February 21.

The Taleban, who since capturing Kabul last September have enforced their purist version of Islam, raided the party, arresting two local employees on the spot and seizing music cassettes, magazines, cameras and photographs.
The other three local staff were arrested later, and the two Frenchmen early the next morning at a United Nations building where they were spending the night.
In court on Wednesday the seven men were accused of a number of crimes, including being in the same house as Afghan women, taking pictures of Afghan women and having music and alcohol at the party.
The United Nations, the OIC and the European Community protested against the arrest of the aid workers and called for their release.
The deputy Secretary General of the OIC, Ibrahim al-Bakr, was in court in Wednesday to hear the verdict. He thanked the Taleban for their leniency.

"The crimes of these young men deserve more punishment according to Islamic law, but because of the Taleban's tolerance and the mediation of the OIC, they have been kind enough to issue this clemency, not only for the two foreigners, but also for the Afghans," said Bakr.
Summing up, the judge told the court the fact that two of the defendants were foreigners had persuaded the court to show clemency.
"Your crimes were very great, but considering that you are expatriates, the court has applied clemency in your case," said Gul.
After the verdict Michel and Llorente told reporters they were thankful for the support they had received and relieved that their ordeal was over.
"We would like to say thank you to everybody for all their support -- to ACF, the OIC and the politicians. It is a bit strange that it is all over, we were not really prepared," said Llorente.
They said they had been generally treated well during the latter stages of their imprisonment.
"Except for the first days, it was almost nice. We had a heater, visits and letters. After the end of the initial interrogation we had very good treatment," said Llorente.
